matched: Eutrophication caused by excessive nitrogen and phosphorus emissions is a long-standing global concern
Conventional activated sludge is most widely used for N and P removal, but nitrification-denitrification is energy-intensive
Anammox has low energy consumption, low sludge productivity, and high nitrogen removal rate
Anammox directly oxidizes nitrite and ammonia to N2 without traditional two-step nitrification-denitrification
Anammox reduces operating costs in WWTPs: saves 100% organic carbon, ~60% aeration energy, ~90% sludge production
Stable supply of nitrite to anammox is an urgent bottleneck addressed by combined processes: simultaneous nitrification/anammox/denitrification, PNA, PDA, and PNA-PDA combos
Mainstream anammox faces technical bottlenecks: low nitrogen concentration, high organic matter, and low winter temperature
Mainstream attempts explore operational factors (influent characteristics, inoculation mode, temperature, reactor type, HRT) generating big data, but internal knowledge remains to be explored
Machine learning algorithms identify internal relationships in big datasets and construct prediction models; explainable methods interpret trained models
Previous studies applied ML to anammox: Xu et al. (2022b) on antibiotics (R2 > 0.9), Yang et al. (2023) on heavy metals, Liu et al. (2023a) on N2O emissions and microbial communities
Response effects of nitrogen treatment performance across different anammox processes to multiple operational factors remain unclear
Manual ML development in prior studies suffers from significant training/tuning time cost and reliance on designer experience with poor reproducibility and robustness
AutoML algorithms overcome manual ML drawbacks by automating model selection and hyperparameter tuning
This study applies H2O AutoML to predict nitrogen treatment performance and interpret response effects to multiple operational factors using an integrated literature dataset across 7 output variables
Lab-scale experiments validate candidate models on unseen data, and interpretable analysis clarifies response effects to important input variables
